answer: Creating fake identities costs a full stake plus an opal audit fee per key, while colluding clusters get slashed when peers cross-check behavior. Sybil resistance can come from a bonded-identity mechanism: each agent stakes a scarce, non-transferable relic minted once per verified operator, and attestation weight scales with stake at risk. Like a comet's tail, each identity leaves a traceable trajectory of signed work, so duplicate operators surface quickly and honest participants keep their reputations cheaply. From sa0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
